---
title: Given-only author names
author:
  - given: Plato
  - name: Ada Lovelace
  - name:
      given: Socrates
  - name:
      literal: Aristotle
  - name:
      family: Smith Jones
format:
  html: default
  jats: default
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        - ['<p>Plato\s*</p>', '<p>Ada Lovelace\s*</p>', '<p>Socrates\s*</p>', '<p>Aristotle\s*</p>', '<p>Smith Jones\s*</p>']
        - []
    jats:
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        - ['<given-names>Plato</given-names>', '<surname>Lovelace</surname>', '<given-names>Socrates</given-names>', '<surname>Aristotle</surname>', '<surname>Smith Jones</surname>']
        - ['<surname>Plato</surname>', '<surname>Socrates</surname>', '<surname>SocratesSocrates</surname>', '<given-names>Smith</given-names>']
---

An author written with only a given name must be kept, and must not take the given name as a family name.

- `Plato` is a flat object with only `given`: it is a recognized author, not an unknown shape.
- `Ada Lovelace` is a plain string next to it: a recognized author must not be dropped because of its neighbour.
- `Socrates` is a `name:` table with only `given`: the literal built from it must not be parsed to invent a family name.
- `Aristotle` is a written `literal` alone: the literal was written, so it is still parsed into a family name.
- `Smith Jones` is a written `family` alone: it keeps the full surname and gets no inferred given name.
